record_type_quote: To assess this association, we performed a replication study in 953 SALS patients and 1039 age- and gender-matched healthy control subjects, who were recruited from Peking University Third Hospital and the First Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University from January 2004 to December 2013 throughout China.

targets.authors: Iida A, Takahashi A, Kubo M, Saito S, Hosono N, Ohnishi Y, et al.
targets.title: A functional variant in ZNF512B is associated with susceptibility to amyotrophic lateral sclerosis in Japanese.
targets.evidence_quote: Recently, Iida et al . performed a large-scale case–control association study using gene-based tag (SNPs) and identified a new SNP (rs2275294) in the ZNF512B gene that is significantly associated with an increased risk of SALS in the Japanese population.[ 25 ]
targets.outcome_quote: In summary, our replication findings did not provide evidence of an association between the variant rs2275294 in the ZNF512B gene and an increased risk of SALS in a Chinese cohort.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly report a negative replication of the susceptibility association. Prognosis was not established as a tested target; Yang et al. appeared during revision and is a comparison rather than the study this attempt was designed to re-test.

reasoning: Independent Chinese case–control sample re-tests the published Japanese susceptibility association.
